title: Visualizing orbital magnetism in electron doped rhombohedral multilayer graphene
claims: The magnetization of the electron-doped quarter metal peaks at finite density in devices with 3 to 15 layers, which the authors attribute to Berry curvature concentrated in a finite-momentum 'ring of fire'.

In a superconducting tetralayer device the zero-resistance state carries a finite out-of-plane (orbital) ferromagnetic moment, giving direct evidence of valley polarization in the superconducting ground state.

Stochastic resistance switching in both metallic and superconducting regimes arises from a density-tuned sign change of the valley-resolved total magnetic moment, which creates metastable magnetic domains.
This sign change can be used to reverse the magnetization of the entire device purely by gate voltage (capacitive reversal).
Any 'condensation magnetization' at the superconducting transition is bounded at no more than 0.1 μB per carrier.
Under an expanded definition (a superconductor coexisting with finite orbital magnetization), the observation is dispositive evidence of chiral superconductivity.
summary: The authors use tilted-tip nanoSQUID-on-tip magnetometry to map the density- and displacement-field-dependent magnetization of electron-doped rhombohedral graphene with 3 to 15 layers, finding a magnetization peak at finite density and gate-driven reversal of macroscopic valley domains that explains stochastic resistance switching. In a superconducting tetralayer they report an out-of-plane moment inside the zero-resistance region and bound any condensation magnetization at 0.1 μB per carrier.
strengths: It is the first local magnetometry inside the zero-resistance region of a proposed chiral superconductor in rhombohedral graphene, a regime transport cannot probe because zero resistance masks the anomalous Hall effect.
A survey of seven devices and six layer numbers gives consistent phase diagrams and shows the finite-density magnetization peak as a generic feature of the electron-doped quarter metal.

Real-space images show nearly uniform gate-driven reversal of the magnetization, tied to transport switching by simultaneous resistance and δB measurements and reproduced in 5L, 6L and a second 13L device.
The technical controls are careful and useful to others: nSOT heating checks, ramp-time statistics of domain formation, electric-field background subtraction and forward-model fringe-field fits.

issues.headline: Magnetized region and zero-resistance region are not shown to coincide
issues.issue: Four-terminal R_xx = 0 needs only one percolating path, the contact pair defining the superconducting contours is not stated, and the ~300 nm probe resolution cannot exclude magnetized normal puddles inside a non-magnetic superconducting network. Fig. 4d shows a non-magnetized upper half within the superconducting window, no local superconducting signature is detected, and the transport dome boundaries come from a different refrigerator and cooldown.

evidence.quote: Correlating transport and local magnetometry data in a superconducting tetralayer sample reveals a finite orbital ferromagnetic moment, providing direct evidence of valley polarization in the superconducting ground state.

issues.fix: Report R_xx for each adjacent voltage-probe pair and show the imaged magnetized segments are at zero resistance; measure the dome boundaries in the nSOT microscope in the same cooldown; measure ΔB versus temperature through T_c at fixed positions, test the domain-averaging reading of Fig. 4d by stabilizing the upper region, compare fitted m with a partial-filling two-component fit, estimate the expected Meissner signal or repeat at larger B⊥, and state the length scale on which coexistence is shown.
issues.fix_scoped: Correlating transport and local magnetometry data in a superconducting tetralayer sample reveals a finite out-of-plane magnetic moment at gate settings where the device shows zero resistance, consistent with valley polarization of the superconducting ground state, although coexistence below the ~0.5 μm resolution of our probe is not established.

edit_scoped.after: Correlating transport and local magnetometry data in a superconducting tetralayer sample reveals a finite out-of-plane magnetic moment at gate settings where the device shows zero resistance, consistent with valley polarization of the superconducting ground state, although coexistence below the ~0.5 μm resolution of our probe is not established.

issues.claim: Valley polarization and orbital moment in the superconductor
issues.headline: Valley polarization evidence is indirect; paper contradicts itself on orbital moment
issues.issue: The abstract, title and Fig. 2 text call the superconductor's moment orbital, but Fig. 4f finds m ≈ 1 μB/carrier with a vanishing orbital part, and a spin-polarized half metal would give the same moment. Valley polarization then rests only on the Methods argument that Ising spin-orbit coupling pins spins out of plane against B∥ = 40 mT, which is not quantified for this WSe₂-free 4L device.

evidence.quote: Collectively, these data may be understood as dispositive evidence of orbital magnetization in both the normal state and the superconducting ground state.
evidence.location: Fig. 2 text; Fig. 4f; Methods (Orbital and spin magnetic moments)

issues.fix: Show a local ΔB hysteresis loop versus B⊥ inside the zero-resistance region with sign reversal and remanence; measure ΔB versus B∥ magnitude and direction; estimate the spin-orbit pinning field for 4L; fit the superconducting images with an in-plane-moment model including the 12.5° tilt; and make the title, abstract, Fig. 2 and Fig. 4 text and Discussion consistent: valley polarization with an orbital contribution consistent with zero.
issues.fix_scoped: Collectively, these data indicate an easy-axis out-of-plane moment, and hence valley polarization, in both the normal state and the superconducting state, with an orbital contribution in the superconductor consistent with zero.

edit_scoped.before: Collectively, these data may be understood as dispositive evidence of orbital magnetization in both the normal state and the superconducting ground state.
edit_scoped.after: Collectively, these data indicate an easy-axis out-of-plane moment, and hence valley polarization, in both the normal state and the superconducting state, with an orbital contribution in the superconductor consistent with zero.

issues.headline: 0.1 μB bound not derived, compares different densities, may constrain nothing
issues.issue: The bound comes from the absence of a step in m at the dome edges in a single density sweep, which compares superconducting and normal points at different densities, has no error bars and scatter comparable to the bound. The measurement temperature is ambiguous (50 mK versus 350 mK), the matched comparison in Fig. 2g covers only 50 and 600 mK and shows 'additional structure', and no predicted size is given.

evidence.quote: For a superconductor in which the Cooper pair condensate carries net angular momentum relative to the normal state, a magnetic signature of the superconducting transition is in principle expected.

issues.fix: Settle the Fig. 4 temperature; extract the bound from ΔB or m at fixed (n_e, D) inside the dome versus temperature from ≥800 mK to 50 mK (or versus B⊥ through H_c2) with simultaneous resistance; state how 0.1 μB/carrier follows with statistical and calibration uncertainties separately; explain the additional structure in Fig. 2g; and give the size predicted by Ref. [5] or a simple estimate.
issues.fix_scoped: Within the ±0.2 μB/carrier point-to-point scatter of a single density sweep at D = 1.02 V/nm, we see no step in m at the edges of the superconducting window.

edit_scoped.before: Our measurement bounds this effect at no more than 0.1μB/carrier, providing a quantitative experimental constraint on theoretical models of valley polarized superconductors[5].
edit_scoped.after: Within the ±0.2 μB/carrier point-to-point scatter of a single density sweep at D = 1.02 V/nm, we see no step in m at the edges of the superconducting window.

issues.claim: Quantitative moments per carrier and the 0.1 μB bound
issues.headline: ΔB-to-m conversion has no uncertainty; superconductor values disagree between figures
issues.issue: All quantitative statements depend on a regularized fringe-field inversion whose tip height is given only as a range, with a 12.5° tilt, and whose regularization, free parameters, reference treatment and residuals are not given. Fig. E2c peaks at ~1 μB/carrier but Fig. E2d (same data as Fig. 4c) at ~2 μB/carrier, and the bistable values in Fig. 4e are not symmetric about zero.

evidence.quote: We then iteratively minimize the residual between the simulated magnetic field and the measured data, with an additional constraint that penalizes gradients of the magnetization to favor smooth solutions.

issues.fix: State the inversion parameters, propagate tip-height and regularization uncertainties into M and m, add error bars to Figs. 1c–d and 4f and every quoted m, explain the E2c/E2d difference, and discuss the asymmetry in Fig. 4e.
issues.fix_scoped: Within the uncertainty of the fringe-field inversion, which is set mainly by the tip height and regularization, the magnetization is of order 1 μB/carrier across the superconducting regime.

edit_scoped.before: This measurement reveals that the magnetization is indistinguishable from 1 μB/carrier across the entire superconducting regime.
edit_scoped.after: Within the uncertainty of the fringe-field inversion, which is set mainly by the tip height and regularization, the magnetization is of order 1 μB/carrier across the superconducting regime.

issues.headline: In-plane spin moment of reference state, seen by tilted tip, ignored
issues.issue: The reference half metal under B∥ has an in-plane spin moment, and the 12.5°-tilted tip is partly sensitive to the in-plane fringe fields it produces at edges; going to a valley-polarized state also rotates the spin out of plane. ΔB thus contains an in-plane term the out-of-plane-only fits omit, which matters most for the small superconducting signal and m ≈ 1 μB/carrier.

evidence.quote: The reference for both images is entirely contained in the valley-balanced half metal with zero magnetic fringe field due to the in-plane applied magnetic field.
evidence.location: Methods (Fig. 4a–b entry); Fig. 2c–d, Fig. E2, Fig. E10b

issues.fix: Estimate the reference-state contribution along the tip's sensing axis, or include an in-plane component in the inversion, and show it does not distort the in-dome signal.
issues.fix_scoped: The reference for both images is entirely contained in the valley-balanced half metal, whose in-plane spin moment may contribute a fringe field along the tilted tip axis that is not included in our out-of-plane fits.

edit_scoped.before: The reference for both images is entirely contained in the valley-balanced half metal with zero magnetic fringe field due to the in-plane applied magnetic field.
edit_scoped.after: The reference for both images is entirely contained in the valley-balanced half metal, whose in-plane spin moment may contribute a fringe field along the tilted tip axis that is not included in our out-of-plane fits.

issues.headline: Electric-field background as large as signal, from mismatched gate configuration
issues.issue: The superconducting-state ΔB is ~0.1 μT while the parasitic electric-field contrast reaches ~±0.25 μT and is removed using a nonmagnetic image at a different D and reference point. Since the background is most sensitive to the top gate and concentrates over contacts, a mis-scaled subtraction could imprint contact-shaped features into the signal.

evidence.quote: This represents the same gate step size away from any magnetic features in the phase diagram. As such, it can be interpreted as purely electric field contrast.

issues.fix: State the top-gate and back-gate voltage steps for both images and show they match, show residual maps for two nonmagnetic configurations with matched steps or the result with two independent background references, and state which subtraction was used in Figs. 2e and 4a–b.
issues.fix_scoped: As such, it is taken as an estimate of the electric field contrast; because it was acquired at a different displacement field, a residual background comparable to the magnetic signal cannot be excluded.

edit_scoped.before: As such, it can be interpreted as purely electric field contrast.
edit_scoped.after: As such, it is taken as an estimate of the electric field contrast; because it was acquired at a different displacement field, a residual background comparable to the magnetic signal cannot be excluded.

issues.headline: Chirality follows from a definition; 'dispositive' is too strong
issues.issue: The chiral-superconductivity conclusion follows from adopting Ref. [33]'s definition and says nothing about order-parameter winding, while coexistence and orbital character are not yet established (concerns 1 and 2). The word 'dispositive' is used both here and for orbital magnetization in the superconducting state.

evidence.quote: Our observation of finite orbital magnetization in both the superconducting and normal states is dispositive evidence of chiral superconductivity under this definition.

issues.fix: Drop 'dispositive'; state in the abstract and Discussion that the data show a superconductor coexisting with valley (and spin) polarization, with chirality in the conventional sense untested, and put the caveat about the expanded definition in the abstract.

issues.issue: The 13L calculation gives ~2 μB/carrier versus ~9–10 μB/carrier measured, a factor of 3–5 not discussed, and uses D, gate distances and ε_r that differ from the experiment. It gives a monotonic positive M_total with no peak or low-density suppression, imposes single-flavor occupancy by hand, and no calculation is shown for 6L.

issues.issue: The switching mechanism rests on a gate-controlled sign change of the single-valley magnetization M_K, drawn only schematically, while the calculated 13L magnetizations in Fig. 1h are positive at all densities shown. The observed reversals near 0.9 and 2.75 × 10¹² cm⁻² are not tied to calculated energetics.

issues.fix: Plot the calculated single-valley M_K(n_e) along the Fig. 3d trajectory and identify where it crosses zero against the observed reversals, ideally also for 5L and 6L.

issues.headline: All superconducting-state magnetometry comes from one device
issues.issue: Magnetism in a superconductor is shown only in device 4L, apparently in one cooldown and one D range; the other devices address only switching, and the 6L device shows no electron-side superconductivity. Whether the images survive thermal cycling is not stated.

evidence.quote: We now return to the magnetic superconducting state in Device 4L.

issues.fix: State the single-device limitation clearly, give the cooldown history of 4L, and if a second superconducting device or thermal cycle is available, show the moment and its anisotropy reproduce.

issues.headline: Heating and sample-temperature statements are inconsistent or unsupported

The ~800 mK label of Fig. 2a is inferred from transport comparisons not shown, although the quarter-metal boundary depends strongly on temperature.

issues.issue: The background plane is fitted to the very low-density portion of each map, exactly where the near-zero or negative M sits. The ΔB→M factor is taken at the peak and assumed constant though domain structure changes at low density, and averaging over field-cooled configurations could suppress M there.

evidence.quote: Along both trajectories shown in Figs 1c-d the total magnetization drops at low densities within the quarter metal, even appearing to go slightly negative.

issues.fix: Show that the low-density M is robust to the choice of background-fit window, and show a spatial image with a fit at a low-density point in the quarter metal demonstrating a uniform domain with small M.
